- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.5) — model tends to overshoot bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (e.g., <0.3) — model fails to capture bearish momentum or mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sharp spikes — adjust for delayed reaction to sentiment shifts.
- After a price spike, model overcorrects downward, then undercorrects — apply smoothing to avoid overshoots in 3–5 day windows.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model often holds prices too high for 2–4 days after a peak, especially when sentiment is high.
- In low-sentiment periods, model underreacts to true price drops — consider adding a 5–10% buffer below forecast for bearish sentiment.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward mid-range values — adjust for sentiment-driven volatility, especially when sentiment >0.6.
